name: mobile-search-target
goal: Search controls retain a 40-pixel target without overlapping revision fields or clipping category labels at every supported viewport.

steps.title: Identify the regression, prior working behavior, root cause, and evidence.
steps.evidence: The existing eight-width search matrix now reaches its geometry assertions after the undefined locator was repaired. At320/390 the actual Search entities button is34px, below its unchanged40px requirement. The mobile responsive selector compresses search/settings with agent icons, and reserves76px=34+8+34. Prior shared EntitySearch targets are40px.

steps.title: Explain why existing standardized tests missed the regression; name the coverage gap and reusable test or shared guard change.
steps.evidence: ui-search-fit.spec.ts is the responsible standardized viewport matrix. An undefined trigger stopped all eight cases before size/overlap checks; Desktop tsconfig excludes tests/e2e, so its normal compiler missed that reference. Reuse this matrix and add height/category-overlap assertions; separately extend normal compiler coverage after the immutable UI pair is recorded. Native readiness and fixture typing repairs were verified against the real native window and phone cases.

steps.title: Strengthen the existing standardized test; commit it before repair, run it failing with loop record --phase red, and preserve the assertion.
Propose a root-cause repair and an automated guard for the identified failure.
Implement the repair and wire the prevention test or guard into normal project verification.
Rerun the same unchanged regression test at a separate fix commit with loop record --phase green; preserve passing proof.
In an isolated fixture or temporary workspace, prove reintroducing the original failure makes the guard fail; restore and prove it passes.

Repeat until the guard and relevant project checks pass; verify affected UI flows with fresh inspected screenshots and no unexpected browser errors; preserve diagnostics and keep pending while proof fails.
